record.original_question: In the six-vertex model on a square lattice with domain wall boundary conditions, the arrows on the upper and lower boundaries point into the lattice while the arrows on the left and right boundaries point out. Determine the bulk correlation functions and the boundary correlation functions for this model, despite the loss of translation invariance caused by the boundary conditions.

evidence.quote: By domain wall boundary conditions we understand the situation in which the arrows on the upper and lower boundaries point in the square lattice and the ones on the left and right boundaries point out.

As in all exactly solvable models the study of correlation functions is of extreme importance. In the case of the six vertex model with DWBC an added difficulty is constituted by the lack of translation invariance.
Open problem: Calculate the bulk and boundary correlation functions of the six vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the six-vertex model on an $N\times N$ square lattice. At each vertex four edges meet, and on each edge an arrow is placed subject to the ice rule: at every vertex exactly two arrows point in and two point out. There are six admissible vertex configurations, to which one assigns Boltzmann weights $a,a,b,b,c,c$ (invariant under reversal of all arrows). Impose domain wall boundary conditions (DWBC): all arrows on the top and bottom external edges point into the lattice, and all arrows on the left and right external edges point out of the lattice. Let $Z_N$ denote the partition function, which is known in closed form as an $N\times N$ Izergin–Korepin determinant.

Because the DWBC break translation invariance, define the following:
(i) Bulk correlation functions: for any finite collection of edges $(e_1,\dots,e_k)$ located in the interior of the lattice (e.g.\ at lattice coordinates that scale with $N$), determine $\langle \sigma_{e_1}\cdots \sigma_{e_k}\rangle_N$, where $\sigma_e\in\{+1,-1\}$ encodes the arrow direction on edge $e$, in the limit $N\to\infty$ with the edges fixed in the rescaled coordinates.
(ii) Boundary correlation functions: determine the analogous multi-point correlation functions for edges located on or adjacent to the boundary of the lattice.

Problem: Obtain explicit (e.g., determinantal or multiple-integral) representations and, where possible, the $N\to\infty$ asymptotics of the bulk and boundary correlation functions of the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions for general values of the weights $a,b,c$ in the disordered, ferroelectric, and antiferroelectric regimes.
artifact.category_tag: Six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: boundary one-point correlation functions have been expressed as $N\times N$ determinants generalizing the Izergin–Korepin formula, and the emptiness formation probability admits determinant and multiple-integral representations via the quantum inverse scattering method. However, a complete description of general bulk and boundary multi-point correlation functions of the six-vertex model with DWBC (especially their large-$N$ asymptotics across all regimes) remains an active research problem rather than a fully solved one.

status_evidence.title: Boundary correlation functions of the six-vertex model
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary one-point correlation functions are expressed as determinants of N×N matrices, generalizing the known result for the partition function.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary one-point functions for DWBC six-vertex model have determinant representations.

status_evidence.title: On the problem of calculation of correlation functions in the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: An approach for calculating correlation functions in the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions via a particular nonlocal correlation function (row configuration probability).
status_evidence.claim: Calculation of general correlation functions in DWBC six-vertex model is an ongoing research problem with partial approaches.

status_evidence.title: Emptiness formation probability in the domain-wall six-vertex model
status_evidence.snippet: The emptiness formation probability allows one to address limit shapes; results given in determinant and multiple-integral form.
status_evidence.claim: Specific nonlocal correlation functions like EFP have been computed.
